vedic_reference.note: Ekalavya is a character in the Mahabharata, a great Indian epic, who was a disciple of Drona, the preceptor of the Pandava princes. Despite being a Shudra, he was a great archer and had the potential to surpass even Arjuna. Drona, however, refused to accept him as a student due to caste prejudice. Ekalavya then made a deal with Drona, vowing to learn the art of archery in secret. He would leave his footprint as a sign of his presence whenever he practiced. When Drona found out, he was impressed by Ekalavya's dedication and skill and accepted him as a student. However, Ekalavya made a promise to Drona that he would not surpass Arjuna, which he kept even when he was much more skilled than Arjuna.
